dlg.keegan.first.0.intent: halts you at the north gate
dlg.keegan.first.0.note: 'Halt!' projected, a touch too loud. Full title, over-articulated. 'Probationary.' a reluctant honesty. 'It is a real title.' defensive.

dlg.keegan.hub.0.note: Schoolmistress; answers herself: 'No? I can tell.'

dlg.keegan.north.0.note: Grave. 'chapter four' with weight she tries not to show.

dlg.keegan.ch4.0.note: A shade too quick; a door shut.

dlg.keegan.prof.0.note: Lecturer's delivery. Rueful about the children. 'That was litotes. You're welcome.' pleased with herself, enunciated.

dlg.keegan.warden.0.intent: the lamps kept the Warden asleep
dlg.keegan.warden.0.note: Sharp '...Who told you that?'. Lecture, gathering seriousness. 'somebody wanted it awake.' cold. Then anxious and small: 'Do not repeat that. I am probationary.'

dlg.keegan.who.0.note: Reasoning aloud; 'you were there' a little accusing.

dlg.keegan.ashe.0.note: Hero-worship. 'with one' quiet. Firm: why she says no.

dlg.keegan.vigil.0.note: Brisk official answer. A pause. The excuse runs on and gets smaller; 'being read by nobody' almost a whisper.

dlg.keegan.ready.0.note: Too honest: 'You would not like it if I saw them.' Then flustered backtracking, a weak joke about paperwork.

dlg.keegan.cb_core_stolen.0.note: Grave, then a pause, then escalating comic determination: 'In capitals.'

dlg.keegan.say_calling.0.note: Delight, deflation, then gossip about the handbook's rudeness.

dlg.keegan.say_calling.2.note: Breaks off 'a ledger of—'. Over-cheerful cover: 'Good morning.' The last question too bright.

dlg.keegan.say_calling.3.note: Prim claim; a pause; honest and small: 'I did not know.'

dlg.keegan.say_calling.4.note: Prim claim; a pause; honest and small: 'I did not know.'

dlg.keegan.dinner.0.note: Prim citation; caught lying; confession; the answer wobbles: 'very nearly no.' Hasty 'Good day.'

dlg.keegan.t_keegan.0.note: Sincere and moving: 'without the bracket.' A pause; comic: the bath, the protest underlining.

dlg.keegan.say_risen.0.note: Narrator for the long look. 'You look well. You look extremely well.' too careful. Then the contraction slips: 'I've got to go' quick and frightened, catching herself 'I— I have to go'. A brittle 'Good day.'
